function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide on where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something ready‑made, custom‑baked, or just a convenient delivery option: | Option | What it offers | How to find it | Tips | |--------|----------------|----------------|------| | **Online cake delivery platforms** | Ready‑made cakes from local bakeries, often delivered same day | • **Amazon Fresh** – has a “Bakery” section with local options.
• **Instacart** – lets you shop at nearby grocery stores that carry cakes.
• **Postmates / DoorDash** – many local bakeries partner with these apps. | Check delivery windows; some services offer “scheduled delivery” so you can pick a time that works for you. | | **Local bakery websites** | Custom orders, seasonal specials, and unique flavors | Search “[city] + bakery” or “custom cake delivery near me.” Many bakeries now have online ordering portals (e.g., **Goldbelly**, **Cake Delivery NYC**). | Look for “delivery” or “take‑out” tabs. Some bakeries also accept phone orders if you prefer a personal touch. | | **Grocery store chains** | Pre‑packaged cakes, birthday boxes, and sometimes custom options | • **Walmart Grocery** – has a “Bakery” section with delivery.
• **Kroger** – offers “Kroger Bakery” with online ordering.
• **Whole Foods** – has a “Bakery” section with delivery via Amazon Fresh. | Great for last‑minute needs; check if they offer “same‑day” delivery. | | **Specialty cake shops** | Gourmet, vegan, gluten‑free, or niche flavors | Search “vegan cake delivery” or “gluten‑free cake shop” plus your city. Examples: **The Cake Shop NYC**, **Vegan Bakehouse**. | These shops often allow you to customize frosting, fillings, and decorations. | | **DIY kits** | Build‑your‑own cake at home | • **Amazon** – “cake baking kit” bundles.
• **Etsy** – handmade cake kits with all ingredients. | Good for a fun activity or when you want full control over ingredients. | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** (ready‑made vs. custom, dietary restrictions, occasion). 2. **Choose a platform** (online delivery app, bakery website, grocery chain). 3. **Browse selections** – most sites let you filter by flavor, size, price, and delivery window. 4. **Place your order** – add any special instructions (e.g., “no nuts,” “birthday message”). 5. **Confirm delivery details** – double‑check address, time slot, and contact info. 6. **Pay securely** – most platforms support credit cards, PayPal, or Apple Pay. ### Extra Tips - **Read reviews**: Look at recent customer photos and comments to gauge quality. - **Check cancellation policies**: Some services charge a fee if you cancel after a certain time. - **Ask about packaging**: For fragile cakes, confirm they use sturdy boxes and proper cushioning. - **Consider local events**: Many bakeries offer “holiday specials” (e.g., pumpkin spice cake in October). If you tell me your city or zip code, I can suggest specific bakeries or delivery services that operate in your area!
